title: Making a Simple Appointment
description: Arrange a simple appointment by checking a day and time.
objectives: Arrange a simple appointment by checking a day and time.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to arrange a simple appointment by checking a day and time. The central language is integrated numbers, dates, time, and availability. It belongs to the practical context of numbers, time & dates. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “Are you available on Friday?” and “Yes, ten o'clock works for me.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: integrated numbers, dates, time, and availability.
